messages:
morgan: saw a weird p99 blip on canary right after the kernel swap, want eyes.
alex: can you paste the perf snippet?
 morgan: here — noticed this at 09:12 UTC during steady load. copied from the topo logs: 
```
[PROFILE] kernel=fast_attn_v3 seq=512 microbatch=4 throughput=120req/s p50=11ms p95=46ms p99=212ms gpu_util=92% kv_miss_rate=0.31
[PROFILE] kernel=fast_attn_v2 seq=512 microbatch=4 throughput=104req/s p50=13ms p95=50ms p99=58ms gpu_util=78% kv_miss_rate=0.05
```
morgan: so the new kernel ups throughput but tail exploded.
rajesh: that p99 >200ms is classic tail amplification when kvcache misses line up with heavier kernel kernels. microbatching 4 may be making the tail worse.
sara: agree — two failure modes: (1) kernel is optimized for long continuous attention and stalls on KV cold paths, (2) high inflight at 92% util leaves zero headroom for spikes (admission can't shed fast).
alex: can we confirm where latency is coming from? nvprof / trace says stall in GEMM switch + memcpy for KV refill?
morgan: nvprof stack attached in cluster logs, shows memcpy+kernel-launch jitter during kv-miss paths. also saw host-side queuing spikes.
natalie: options: reduce microbatch from 4->2 (lower util but fewer coalesced misses), add proactive KV prefetch for top prefixes, or add soft-admit that caps target_gpu_util at ~80%. each has tradeoffs on throughput/cost.
rajesh: propose an ABX test on canary:
  A) revert kernel to v2 (control)
  B) keep v3 + kv-prefetch + no admit changes
  C) keep v3 + kv-prefetch + soft-admit with util_cap=0.82 + microbatch=3
sara: also add p95/p99 synthetic probes (short chat bursts) to exercise KVMISS hot paths; log kv_miss_rate and admit decisions per request.
morgan: i'll run those three configs tomorrow morning. @ci-bot can you enqueue perf jobs and include nvprof, kernel histograms, and per-request admit logs?
ci-bot: perf job queued: perf-canary-2291234578. configs A/B/C scheduled across 3 nodes. will post results to thread when complete. :rocket:
alex: quick note — for chat-style workloads aim for lower steady util target (70-80%) because tail sensitivity is higher than throughput. 90%+ means tight coupling to kv warmup behavior.
morgan: acknowledged, will capture headroom metric = (1 - observed_util) and correlate with p99.
natalie: if soft-admit helps, let's also simulate sudden spike with synthetic users to validate shedding doesn't cause error amplification.
morgan: thanks all — will share raw traces + summary once jobs finish. tagging followups in #eng-runtime-sync if we need rollout hold.
